Review Body:
Review of The Body Keeps the Score by Bessel van der Kolk

I came to this book at precisely the right moment in my life, thanks to the recommendation of my naturopathic doctor, Taggy Bensaid. At the time, I was about six months into therapy for my own PTSD and just beginning to explore deeper healing approaches. This book became a guidepost, illuminating the intersections of trauma, healing, and the holistic therapies I was already embracing, like music, massage, and yoga.

One of the most powerful lessons I took from this book is the understanding that many behaviors—especially in children—aren’t willful defiance or laziness, but expressions of unprocessed trauma. It reinforced my belief that society, as a whole, has a responsibility to address the growing epidemic of trauma, not just by treating individuals but by creating environments that foster healing and growth.

This resonated deeply with me as both a teacher and a choir member. It explained why I’ve struggled with breathing properly in choir and gave me tools to approach teaching with more compassion—not as a disciplinarian, but as someone committed to understanding what’s happening in a child’s world before taking action.

On a personal level, this book affirmed my vision for strengthening connections within my extended family. Too often, I’ve encountered resistance in the form of phrases like, “People have to take care of their own families,” or “You can’t make people do what they don’t want to do.” This book helped me see those responses in a new light, rooted in their own unprocessed experiences, and gave me renewed determination to move beyond that negativity.

The Body Keeps the Score isn’t just a book—it’s a lifeline for anyone seeking to understand trauma and chart a path toward healing. It’s accessible, insightful, and profoundly validating, and I’m grateful to have encountered it at such a pivotal time in my life.
